newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Bundesbank's Meister welcomes UK stance on Europe.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank's Meister welcomes UK stance on Europe.

text.p: Bundesbank board member Edgar Meister welcomed Monday the attitude of Britain's new Labour government towards Europe, saying it was positive for the success of plans for a single currency.

Asked whether Labour's triumph in Britain's May 1 election would contribute positively to the European Union, Meister told a banking conference in Argentina: "I think so. I think that the main advantages of the single currency will come about when the greatest number of countries possible take part. Therefore, it is at least positive that Britain has found new relations with Europe."
Meister said Britain was seeking a "new relationship" with the single currency and said: "I am convinced it will find a reply to this search."

He went on to say that British membership in the single currency planned for introduction in January 1999 would enrich the project. "British membership in the single currency would strengthen the euro," he said.
British membership would also raise the consensus in favor of the single currency, Meister said.
The new government of Labour Prime Minister Tony Blair is seen as being more open to cooperation with its European Union partners than the previous Conservative government of John Major.

Labour plans to sign Britain up to the EU's Social Chapter on workers' rights and the new Foreign Secretary Robin Cook has said Britain should join a single currency if it is a success, though he declined to fix a specific date. He pledged Britain would help facilitate the introduction of the euro.
